item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-c5364db15f17cf08","start_unit":16,"end_unit":20,"fact_summary":"The Supreme Court’s case record states that the Guardia Nacional law was enacted in 2019, while the CNDH alleged that it omitted specific rules for federal-state/municipal coordination, local contributions, and performance evaluation, creating legal uncertainty and potential arbitrariness. These omissions were presented as defects in legislation enacted during López Obrador’s administration.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","4B.2","4B.4","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The Court decided the case in April 2023 concerning a 2019 law; it is relevant to the institutional posture inherited and operating during 2023, but does not establish a new 2023 policy decision by López Obrador.","ruler_attribution":"The challenged law was enacted during López Obrador’s presidency; the record attributes the legislative omissions to Congress and reports the Executive’s defense, not a personal order by López Obrador.","limitations":["The cited units summarize the CNDH’s allegations and do not by themselves establish that López Obrador personally directed each omission."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c5364db15f17cf08","start_unit":95,"end_unit":105,"fact_summary":"The Court described the Guardia Nacional’s statutory design as a civil, disciplined, professional security institution governed by legality, objectivity, efficiency, professionalism, probity, and respect for human rights; it included career certification, annual evaluation, weapons training and controls, disciplinary rules, ministerial control of criminal investigations, Senate reporting, judicial oversight of communications, and federal funding, with local contributions and capacity-building programs through agreements.","question_ids":["1B.3","1B.7","1B.10","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.6","4B.4","5B.6","6B.4","6B.9","8B.2","8B.3","8B.4","8B.5","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"These statutory safeguards were in force and relevant to the 2023 institutional framework.","ruler_attribution":"The framework was enacted during López Obrador’s administration, but the cited material describes statutory institutions and does not identify his personal implementation choices.","limitations":["The document describes formal design rather than measured implementation or outcomes in 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c5364db15f17cf08","start_unit":125,"end_unit":136,"fact_summary":"The Court held that the law provided temporary federal-state/municipal coordination, formal requests and agreements, local responsibilities, funding and capacity-building programs with monitoring indicators, and career evaluation through certification, training, annual reviews, promotion criteria, personnel records, and a career council.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.4","3B.6","4B.4","5B.6","6B.4","6B.9","8B.2","8B.3","8B.4","8B.5","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The ruling was issued in April 2023 and assessed the statutory framework applicable during the target year.","ruler_attribution":"This is a judicial finding about legislation enacted during López Obrador’s presidency; it does not independently show personal execution by López Obrador.","limitations":["The Court assessed legal sufficiency, not whether all programs, evaluations, and indicators operated effectively in practice."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c5364db15f17cf08","start_unit":156,"end_unit":168,"fact_summary":"The Court upheld the Guardia Nacional’s authority to conduct preventive crime research without ministerial direction before a criminal proceeding, while requiring legality, objectivity, efficiency, professionalism, probity, and human-rights compliance; criminal investigations after a suspected offense remain under prosecutorial direction.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.5","3B.6","3B.9","4B.9","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"This legal interpretation was binding in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The authority derives from legislation enacted during López Obrador’s presidency; the ruling does not show that he personally ordered a particular investigation.","limitations":["The decision establishes the legal boundary but provides no case-specific evidence of compliance or abuse."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c5364db15f17cf08","start_unit":171,"end_unit":188,"fact_summary":"The Court treated generalized preventive information gathering and internet monitoring as non-coercive intelligence functions, but required respect for privacy, presumption of innocence, and exclusion of private or legally protected information; the Court nevertheless recorded dissenting concerns about the breadth of these powers.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.6","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The statutory interpretation governed the 2023 legal environment.","ruler_attribution":"The powers were created under legislation enacted during López Obrador’s presidency; the cited judicial reasoning does not attribute operational use to him personally.","limitations":["The majority’s legal characterization and the dissenting concerns are both included; the record does not establish actual surveillance practices in 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c5364db15f17cf08","start_unit":179,"end_unit":188,"fact_summary":"The Court invalidated the statutory authority for undercover and simulated-user operations because it lacked sufficiently specific conditions, a crime catalogue, and prior judicial control, creating risks of arbitrary use, privacy violations, self-incrimination, and tainted evidence.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","4B.9","7B.6","8B.2","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The invalidation was issued in April 2023 and therefore directly affected the target-year legal framework.","ruler_attribution":"The invalidated provision was enacted during López Obrador’s administration; the ruling does not establish that he personally authorized an undercover operation.","limitations":["The ruling concerns statutory authority and does not document a specific operation or resulting victim."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c5364db15f17cf08","start_unit":188,"end_unit":206,"fact_summary":"The Court upheld statutory communications-intervention powers based on judicial authorization, specified applications, a limited catalogue of serious offenses, time limits, inventories, judicial verification and revocation, destruction of non-useful information, confidentiality duties, and certified personnel; several justices dissented, arguing that preventive interception was unconstitutional and risked subjective profiling.","question_ids":["1B.3","1B.8","1B.9","3B.4","3B.5","4B.9","7B.6","8B.2","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The majority ruling was binding in 2023, while the dissents qualify the legal and rights-risk assessment.","ruler_attribution":"The statutory scheme was enacted during López Obrador’s presidency; the record does not show personal requests for interception by López Obrador.","limitations":["The record establishes formal safeguards and judicial disagreement, not actual implementation or misuse in 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c5364db15f17cf08","start_unit":207,"end_unit":209,"fact_summary":"The Court did not invalidate the Guardia Nacional’s real-time mobile geolocation authority because the required qualified majority was not reached; the disposition therefore did not affirm the provision’s constitutionality, and seven justices voted for invalidation.","question_ids":["1B.3","1B.9","3B.5","4B.9","7B.6","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The unresolved constitutional status was part of the legal environment in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The authority originated in legislation enacted during López Obrador’s administration; no personal use by him is shown.","limitations":["The procedural dismissal for lack of votes is not a merits holding that the power was lawful or unlawful."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c5364db15f17cf08","start_unit":218,"end_unit":218,"fact_summary":"The Court’s final disposition recognized the validity of the communications-intervention provisions, but the cited vote count shows that the reasoning was not supported by a broad consensus and several justices opposed the result.","question_ids":["1B.3","1B.8","3B.4","3B.5","4B.9","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"This was the final 2023 disposition of the challenged safeguards.","ruler_attribution":"The disposition concerned a statute enacted during López Obrador’s presidency, not a personal judicial or operational act by him.","limitations":["The vote count does not itself demonstrate implementation or harm."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c5364db15f17cf08","start_unit":218,"end_unit":218,"fact_summary":"The Court held that Guardia Nacional migration inspections and presentations must be performed subordinately to the Instituto Nacional de Migración, under its guidelines; the Guardia Nacional may support migrant accommodation and station security only at the Institute’s request.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.7","3B.9","4B.4","6B.3","6B.8","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The interpretation was binding during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The migration authority was established by legislation enacted during López Obrador’s administration; the record does not show his personal direction of individual migration actions.","limitations":["The holding supplies legal constraints, but not evidence of actual compliance or conditions in migrant facilities."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c5364db15f17cf08","start_unit":218,"end_unit":218,"fact_summary":"The Court’s migration holding treated irregular status as insufficient by itself to establish criminal conduct and required objective, reasonable, necessary, proportionate, and rights-respecting grounds for restrictions, while acknowledging dissenting concerns that the statutory wording could enable autonomous or discriminatory inspections.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.7","3B.8","3B.9","4B.3","4B.7","4B.9","6B.3","6B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"These legal standards applied in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The standards concern statutory powers enacted during López Obrador’s presidency, not a demonstrated personal statement or order by him.","limitations":["The source contains both the majority’s limiting interpretation and dissenting objections; it does not establish operational discrimination."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c5364db15f17cf08","start_unit":272,"end_unit":272,"fact_summary":"The Court upheld migrant-station security powers only as subordinate assistance to the Instituto Nacional de Migración, with founded and motivated requests, application of migration-law rules, and respect for migrants’ human rights; it treated the underlying accommodation decision as an INM decision rather than a Guardia Nacional decision.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.7","3B.9","4B.4","6B.3","6B.8","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The ruling defined the applicable framework during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The legal arrangement was enacted during López Obrador’s presidency; no personal involvement in a particular station or migrant case is shown.","limitations":["The Court reviewed the statute abstractly and did not determine whether migrant-station conditions or individual practices complied."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c5364db15f17cf08","start_unit":272,"end_unit":272,"fact_summary":"The Court invalidated the blanket requirement that Guardia Nacional applicants have never been convicted of any offense, finding it overbroad because it did not distinguish intentional from negligent, serious from minor, recent from old, completed from ongoing, or job-related from unrelated offenses, and could stigmatize people after reintegration.","question_ids":["3B.7","4B.7","4B.10","6B.8","7B.10","8B.2","8B.8"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The invalidation took effect after notification in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The requirement was enacted during López Obrador’s presidency, while the corrective action was taken by the Supreme Court; the source does not show whether López Obrador supported or opposed the requirement.","limitations":["The Court separately desisted for lack of a qualified majority on other challenged eligibility requirements."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c5364db15f17cf08","start_unit":309,"end_unit":325,"fact_summary":"The Court held that the Guardia Nacional disciplinary framework included complaint escalation, written and reasoned disciplinary orders, proportionality criteria, presumption of innocence, public hearings, defense counsel, evidence and arguments, recusals, and an appeal mechanism through the regulation.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","4B.4","4B.9","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"These procedural safeguards were recognized as applicable in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The framework was enacted and regulated during López Obrador’s administration; the judicial record does not establish personal supervision by him.","limitations":["The Court’s holding concerns legal availability of procedures, not their accessibility or effectiveness in individual cases."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c5364db15f17cf08","start_unit":329,"end_unit":353,"fact_summary":"The Court upheld the Guardia Nacional’s explicit duty not to inflict or tolerate torture, cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment, or enforced disappearance, including under superior orders, and held that violations could trigger administrative, criminal, civil, political, removal, suspension, dismissal, or disqualification consequences under multiple laws.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.9","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.2","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The statutory duty and Court ruling were operative in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The duty was enacted during López Obrador’s presidency, but the source does not document his personal enforcement or correction of a specific abuse.","limitations":["The Court addressed the legal framework and sanctions, not actual incidence, investigation, or remedy of abuses in 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c5364db15f17cf08","start_unit":354,"end_unit":381,"fact_summary":"The Court upheld a disciplinary restriction allowing the Guardia Nacional to keep personnel at their assigned installations and available to superiors without free time for up to eight or fifteen days, viewing it as a proportionate discipline measure; multiple justices dissented that it materially restricted liberty, could be imposed without prior hearing, and was more severe than necessary.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","4B.3","4B.4","7B.7","8B.2","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The measure and its constitutional treatment applied in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The disciplinary measure was enacted during López Obrador’s presidency; the record does not show that he personally imposed it.","limitations":["The source records a divided judicial assessment and does not show frequency, implementation, or individual harms."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c5364db15f17cf08","start_unit":398,"end_unit":401,"fact_summary":"The final judgment declared invalid the undercover-operation power and the blanket no-conviction eligibility rule; it upheld numerous other provisions, including preventive investigation, specified communications safeguards, subordinate migration assistance, disciplinary rules, torture prohibitions, and weapons-custody provisions, while dismissing several challenges for failure to reach the qualified vote threshold.","question_ids":["1B.3","1B.8","3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.7","4B.4","4B.9","6B.8","7B.6","8B.2","8B.6","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"This was the Court’s operative 2023 disposition.","ruler_attribution":"The judgment reviewed legislation enacted during López Obrador’s presidency and constrained parts of that framework; it does not establish personal action by López Obrador beyond the administration’s institutional role.","limitations":["Qualified-vote dismissals do not resolve the underlying constitutional merits."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The supplied source is a judicial decision and related opinions about the Guardia Nacional law; it provides substantial legal and institutional evidence but little direct evidence of López Obrador’s personal statements, appointments, budgets, operational compliance, corruption, economic policy, social welfare, international peace, or existential-risk policy in 2023.","The source contains majority holdings, dissents, concurrences, party submissions, and arguments; polarity reflects the evidentiary content and does not constitute a score.","Formal legal safeguards are not treated as proof of effective implementation or outcomes."]}
